Usage: drive <command> [flags]

drive runs Claude Code sessions in Rex for their owner: read where each stands, send its next step, answer its prompts, and be woken when its turn ends.

The driver stands in for the sessions' owner, usually while they are away:
a chat bot woken by webhook, or a Claude Code session. A batch is one
drive's sessions and its record; `drive batch new NAME` starts one.

Every action on a session is decided on a VIEW, such as T1@3fa91c07, which
read, wait, status and every wake print. The action is refused once the
session has moved past that view, so a step decided on an old turn never
reaches a new one. A working session's view changes as it writes: decide on
a turn that has ended, or send with --queue. One driver acts on a session at
a time.

A SESSION is a label in the batch (T1), or a session's Rex block id, whose
last six characters are enough, before it joins the batch; its view starts
the same way (7c1e2a@3fa91c07). Copy a view as drive printed it.

A refusal or failure that leaves something to do ends with a next: line: a
command that runs as written on the session as it stands. Whether the step
still makes sense is the driver's judgment.

Flags:
  -h, --help          Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME    Act in this batch instead of the current one, which stays current. It may
                      stand anywhere on the line.

Commands:
  status                             Print every session in the batch, live: its state, stage, pull
                                     request, wake and view.
  read <session>                     Print a session's newest reply, where it stands, its view, and
                                     next: where its state decides it.
  wait <session>                     Block until a session's turn ends, then print how it ended.
  send <view> [<line> ...]           Send a session its next step, decided on a view.
  open <label> [<line> ...]          Open a new Claude Code session in Rex, in the batch, with an
                                     optional first step.
  respond <view> <action>            Answer the prompt a session waits on.
  watch [<session>]                  Arm a session's wake in a batch that wakes a chat driver; --due
                                     arms every one that needs it.
  timer <seconds> <note> ...         Wake the driver after a delay, with a note: a veto window, a
                                     check that is due later.
  park <view> <reason> ...           Stop a session's wakes until a step is sent to it, keeping why.
  close <view>                       Close a session's block after its last step.
  record grant --source=SOURCE --scope=SCOPE
                                     Record authority the owner handed over, in their words, with
                                     what it covers.
  record ask --question=QUESTION --if-unanswered=IF-UNANSWERED <session>
                                     Record a question put to the owner, with its recommendation and
                                     what happens unanswered.
  record answer --took=TOOK <ask>    Record the owner's answer to an ask.
  record note <text> ...             Record a note, such as the plan, for the run after a reset to
                                     read.
  log                                Print the batch's timeline: what was sent, answered, opened,
                                     parked and closed, and every wake.
  metrics                            Print the batch's measures: asks and the owner's wait, merges,
                                     sends, wakes, refusals.
  batch show                         Print the batch: its start, wakes, Rex session, zone, sessions
                                     and directory (default).
  batch new <name>                   Start a batch and make it current.
  batch use <name>                   Make a batch current.
  batch list                         List every batch, the current one starred.
  snippet <key> [<dir>] [<text> ...]
                                     Print the owner's snippet KEY as a session in DIR would receive
                                     it.
  snippets [<dir>]                   List the snippet keys that resolve in DIR, each with its file.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner

Run "drive <command> --help" for a command's details.
